briefs.title: Paraguay Ousts Its President, Sudan Accuses Ethiopia, Iran Faces a Winter Gas Crisis
briefs.bluf: This edition was rebuilt around what most outlets missed. Paraguay's Senate removed President Santiago Peña 44 to 0 after a bank collapse froze deposits for nearly half the country, putting one of Taiwan's last allies in flux. Sudan formally accused Ethiopia at the UN of hosting RSF drone launches, as Ethiopia's own war reignites on three fronts and an Ebola outbreak in Congo passes 10,700 cases with spread to Kenya and Nigeria. In the Gulf, Iran faces a winter gas shortfall and is executing protesters while it negotiates, the Houthis are licensing Red Sea shipping by email, and Gulf fertilizer and sulphur exports are down about 70%, a food and metals shock that will hit after the oil headlines fade. In Washington, Stephen Miller becomes chief of staff Monday and a judge threw out the DOJ suit against Alaska's Senate certification.
briefs._s: paraguay ousts its president, sudan accuses ethiopia, iran faces a winter gas crisis this edition was rebuilt around what most outlets missed. paraguay's senate removed president santiago peña 44 to 0 after a bank collapse froze deposits for nearly half the country, putting one of taiwan's last allies in flux. sudan formally accused ethiopia at the un of hosting rsf drone launches, as ethiopia's own war reignites on three fronts and an ebola outbreak in congo passes 10,700 cases with spread to kenya and nigeria. in the gulf, iran faces a winter gas shortfall and is executing protesters while it negotiates, the houthis are licensing red sea shipping by email, and gulf fertilizer and sulphur exports are down about 70%, a food and metals shock that will hit after the oil headlines fade. in washington, stephen miller becomes chief of staff monday and a judge threw out the doj suit against alaska's senate certification. stephen miller becomes white house chief of staff after the midterm loss trump named stephen miller chief of staff starting november 9, replacing susie wiles. trump frames it as wiles moving to his political operation; zerohedge highlights a claim on joe rogan's show that her office signed off on nearly every major decision. judge throws out doj suit to hold up alaska's senate certification judge sharon gleason ruled doj lacked standing in united states v. alaska. doj wanted ballots set aside while it checked whether votes for a second 'daniel j. sullivan' were meant for sen. dan sullivan. she found ballots already mixed and impossible to separate without breaking ballot secrecy. doj reportedly opens a grand jury probe into the dobbs leak the dc us attorney's office under jeanine pirro is reportedly subpoenaing people who worked at the supreme court in 2022. the court's own 2023 inquiry never found the leaker. the report builds on a november 5 new york times story with anonymous sources. a 181 page progressive memo tells democrats to subpoena ceos, not just the white house the groundwork collaborative wants hearings with landlords on junk fees, sports betting apps on addiction, grocers on surveillance pricing and ai firms. rep. greg casar wants ai ceos first; the centrist progressive policy institute is pushing back. wealth taxes lose in california but move forward in washington and colorado california's one time 5% billionaire tax was trailing about 56 to 44, and a measure banning such taxes was winning. repeal of washington's 9.9% tax on income over $1 million was failing; a colorado millionaire surtax was narrowly ahead. voters rejected data centers in 38 of 40 plus local races six cities banned data centers outright and 12 capped their power draw. mayors who backed hyperscale projects lost in yukon, oklahoma (a recall) and burgin, kentucky. dc's socialist mayor elect walks into a federal collision janeese lewis george will run a city where congress can veto laws and approve the budget, the national guard is deployed and there is a $1.1 billion gap. the aclu of dc wants a local law letting residents sue federal officers who violate their rights. iran hangs two isfahan protesters; two more death sentences in mashhad amirhossein maleki and amirhossein ebrahimi, sentenced over the january protests, were hanged. a single source told iran international that maleki went through a staged hanging after retracting his confession. iran human rights counts at least 36 protesters executed since march. gas rich iran faces a winter shortage and leans on russia the national gas company says about 130 million cubic meters a day, roughly 16% of last year's output, is still offline after the march strikes. about 11 provinces could face shortages. hardliners float leaving the nuclear treaty; the atomic chief attacks the iaea head after the us midterms, hardline commentators say a democratic congress changes nothing and propose threatening to leave the npt; hamshahri printed a map of us bases in europe. atomic energy chief mohammad eslami called iaea head rafael grossi an agent of iran's enemies. kurdish government splits: puk quits after kdp seats a speaker without it kurdistan's parliament met for the first time in almost two years and elected kdp's vala farid speaker with the puk boycotting. puk leader bafel talabani says if the kdp appoints regional leaders alone, the puk will appoint its own in sulaymaniyah. us reportedly threatens to label iraq a state sponsor of terrorism over militia weapons unnamed sources say the us chargé told baghdad it could face sanctions and the label without a concrete plan to bring militia weapons under state control by june 30, 2027. the militias' conditions include us and turkish troops leaving and the kurdish peshmerga being dissolved. the houthis are issuing red sea transit permits by email since declaring a blockade of saudi arabia, the houthis have answered ships' emailed requests for safe passage, usually within 24 hours, per a wsj investigation. one chinese container ship got a seven day permit and an offer of houthi alerts. aramco profit up 34.6% as it plans a bigger hormuz bypass pipeline aramco's third quarter net profit rose to $36.2 billion, and the ceo said engineering has begun to expand the east west pipeline to the red sea from 7 to 10 million barrels a day. saudi arabia signs a defense pact and $403 million in deals with syria after ahmed al sharaa's second riyadh trip in a month, the saudis funded health centers, 10,000 home repairs, water systems and aleppo's power plant, and the defense ministries signed a cooperation agreement. documents tie press tv's london office to the sovereign media network correspondence shows press tv london paid ahmed kaballo about £41,700, partly in cash via the embassy. kaballo founded african stream, which the state department says rt secretly ran, and now leads sovereign, which reuses press tv content and contributors. hebron siege lifted after election week as october set a record for settler attacks the army withdrew from hebron on november 2 after a closure that displaced about 5,000 people; the governor puts losses at 10 to 12 million shekels a day in a city that makes about 40% of palestinian industrial output. ocha counted 397 damaging settler attacks in 26 days of october, the most since 2006. egypt's army uses armed drones on gold miners at the sudan border, arrests 691 the army says it arrested 151 egyptians and 540 foreigners and confirmed using armed drones; a rights group blames an october air strike on a border mine that killed at least 72 miners. the kyiv 'torture house' clash: part real grievance, part influence op about 200 people stormed a national guard transit house near kyiv holding mobilized men and deserters; officers used tear gas and warning shots. the woman who set it off posing as a medic was a cosmetologist and has been detained. ukraine's anticorruption bureau closes the midas probe; an sbu official threatened a gun during searches nabu finished its investigation into the mindich energy kickback scheme, alleging 10 to 15% skimmed from energoatom contracts and over $111 million laundered. in another case nabu says a senior sbu official obstructed searches and threatened to use a firearm; sbu special forces showed up and the acting sbu chief fired two officials. putin ratifies a deal letting bailiffs pull bank data on russians abroad russian bailiffs can now ask kazakhstan, belarus, azerbaijan, kyrgyzstan, tajikistan and uzbekistan where a debtor lives, works and banks, without notifying them. drone force recruiters found at 49 of russia's top 50 universities novaya gazeta europe and molniya found recruiting at 228 universities in 79 regions; students with poor grades face shortened retake deadlines and threats of expulsion followed by conscription. st petersburg cuts its army sign up bonus nearly ninefold the city cut its bonus from 3.5 million rubles to 400,000, its second cut in two weeks; mari el and mordovia did the same, and the defense ministry proposed pushing december pay into january. inside kiriyenko's propagandist training pipeline the 'new media workshop', run through sanctioned dialog regiony and linked to the doppelgänger operation, claims 1,700 graduates staffing rt, solovyov live and outlets in occupied ukraine. kremlin source: putin saw the finnish and norwegian call as an opening to europe per farida rustamova's vlast newsletter, putin views finland and norway as softer than berlin, paris and london; both want a standing channel, and kyiv coordinated the october 26 call. armenia's opposition unites after billionaire karapetyan's arrest the russian armenian billionaire and 35 associates were jailed; hours later opposition groups formed an alliance against constitutional changes baku demands before signing the peace treaty. georgia's ruling party moves to limit election challenges; russia bans a pro european party watchdogs warn a georgian dream bill limits challenges to final results to technical errors and scraps random recounts. the same day russia declared the opposition party droa undesirable. us licenses hungary's mol to start taking serbia's nis refinery from russia ofac allowed mol initial steps, transfer of russian origin securities and russian approvals, but not closing; budapest expects a deal by december 11. china's top military command is down to two men after the plenum purge after the fifth plenum expelled 33 members, 16 of them military, only xi jinping and zhang shengmin hold seats on the seven seat central military commission. the plenum also told provincial bosses to speak last in meetings and curbed demands for personal loyalty; retired general wang ning was removed from the top advisory body november 5. beijing passes a cross border anticorruption law with global reach the npc standing committee passed a law giving beijing new tools to chase offshore assets; earlier drafts also aimed to counter foreign corruption probes of chinese firms. a wuhan court is hearing a $53.5 billion covid 'defamation' suit against missouri chinese authorities and research institutes sued the us state of missouri over covid claims, and hearings began. china's central bank brakes the yuan with its first fx reserve hike in five years banks' foreign currency reserve requirement rises from 4% to 6% on november 15, locking up an estimated $20 to 25 billion. the yuan had risen 14 sessions straight; it then fell to a two week low. new zealand votes today with a 6% party holding the balance the final 1news verian poll had national 30, labour 29, greens 16, act 10, nz first 8 and the opportunity party 6.2, leaving both blocs short of 61 seats. unemployment hit 5.7%, an 11 year high. indonesia busts a ring trafficking its citizens into russia's army police arrested 13 suspects, including two russians and a ukrainian, with 58 alleged victims recruited through tiktok and facebook ads and sent on tourist visas. jakarta formally asked moscow to stop recruiting indonesians. north korea rehearses knocking out allied airbases, with doctored photos kcna reported anti aircraft missile tests and a cruise missile dropping cluster munitions on a mock runway; nk news found the images heavily manipulated. border loudspeakers are installed but silent. pyongyang's quiet diplomatic thaw before apec kim jong un's international department chief went to beijing ten days after kim visited dandong; brazil's first ambassador in a decade took up his post. kim yo jong said talks with the us are possible but not necessary and rejected the fbi's attribution of the $6.3 billion binance theft. thailand triples tax on imported evs as chinese competition bites the cabinet raised excise on imported battery evs from 10% to 35% starting january to protect local manufacturing. pakistan's ousted provincial chief is still missing as the coalition cracks since emergency rule in khyber pakhtunkhwa on october 11, former chief minister sohail afridi and two pti lawmakers are in 'protective custody' and 200 plus public order cases were filed. coalition partner bilawal bhutto told the government to stop fighting everyone; jui-f protested alleged drone surveillance of fazlur rehman's home. havana reportedly met us officials in new york the day its foreign minister denied talks martí noticias, citing anonymous sources, reports vice minister carlos fernández de cossío led an unannounced meeting with us officials during the un general assembly on september 24, the same day bruno rodríguez told ap no meetings were planned. barbados pm: cuba needs food and power before talk of political change mia mottley told cnn cuba must first secure food and energy, and this time did not blame the embargo. paraguay's senate removes president santiago peña, who is detained at home the senate voted 44 to 0 to remove peña for poor performance after the central bank took over ueno bank, freezing deposits for about 3 million clients, close to half the country. prosecutors accuse him of favoring a bank he had business ties to, including with public pension money. vice president pedro alliana serves until 2028. venezuela bombs an eln camp, breaking 20 years of chavista tolerance government drones hit an eln guerrilla camp in apure, apparently with a cocaine lab, killing at least 19; the nyt reported us help. machado and gonzález back a us plan: new courts first, elections within six months the state department plan would name new supreme court and electoral council members by year end, declare the presidency vacant, then hold a vote within six months, possibly july 24. venezuela's reserves fall despite $90 oil oikos research finds prices up 245% since december while the bolívar fell 198%, and the central bank lost a net $608 million in reserves; the budget assumed $55 oil. venezuela softens its hate law: prison out, dollar fines in a first reading replaces 10 to 20 year sentences with fines of 500 to 10,000 times the dollar rate; press unions want repeal and 140 web domains stay blocked. nicaragua drops cuban and venezuelan troops from its 2027 military permits but keeps russia decree 13/2026 lists foreign forces allowed in for exercises; for the first time since 2020 cuba and venezuela are out, russia keeps the largest quota. bukele's 2,000 troops in haiti operate outside the un force about 2,000 salvadoran soldiers with armor and air support deployed after an october ambush; the un says most sit outside the gang suppression force. a gang boss wrote to the un seeking a truce. colombia's forensic institute pushes back on soldiers moving bodies after combat medicina legal asked that troops be barred from moving bodies or belongings on their own under a draft decree on deaths in security operations. mexico's election authority files a criminal complaint after its chair quits the ine asked prosecutors to investigate former chair guadalupe taddei, who resigned over ties to a contractor; about 30 senior staff have left and all contracts, including voter id production, are under review. the ai fake id kingpin is free and explains how he beat bank checks yuriy nazarenko's onlyfake sold more than 10,000 ai generated ids at about $15 each, used by north korean fake it workers; he pleaded guilty, served about a year and left the us. ice moving to deport up to 80 afghans, including people who aided us forces the free press profiles a former kabul police officer who worked with us troops, now held in louisiana; 66 democratic lawmakers asked rubio to cancel the flights, reportedly routed through pakistan. sudan takes ethiopia to the un security council over rsf drones launched from ethiopian soil khartoum cites 70 attacks with 187 one way drones from february to october, 28 in october alone, killing 176 soldiers; it names asosa airport, the kurmuk border area and bahir dar airbase as launch sites. addis says sudan's army backs tplf linked rebels. ethiopia's old enemies now fight together: fano cuts the a2 highway amhara fano fighters reportedly took ibnat and cut parts of the a2 between dessie and woldia, addis ababa's supply line north, while federal forces push toward sheraro in tigray. tplf and fano leaders released a joint video vowing to overthrow the government. fighting over moyale pushes about 50,000 people into kenya; grenades hit a kenyan school ethiopian somalis and oromos have fought over moyale since october 18; on november 1 three rpgs fired from ethiopia hit a primary school in kenyan moyale. somalia's supreme court strikes down the president's term extension a day after he fired the chief justice the court ruled hassan sheikh mohamud's one year extension unlawful and that his term ended in may; he had dismissed chief justice bashe yusuf ahmed the night before. uganda will pull all its troops out at the end of next year. nigerian court voids atiku's opposition nomination ten weeks before the vote the federal high court threw out the adc leadership under david mark, and atiku abubakar's nomination fell with it; the adc will appeal and blames the ruling apc, which denies a role. guinea expels more than 8,000 burkinabè gold miners expulsions followed a ban on artisanal mining in northeast guinea; burkina's security minister says miners were injured and killed and ouagadougou got no notice. tanzania acquits tundu lissu of treason but jails him four years for incitement the opposition leader, held 19 months, was cleared of the capital charge and convicted of a lesser one he was never charged with. bundibugyo ebola passes 10,700 confirmed cases, with spread to kenya and nigeria as of november 4, drc had 10,741 confirmed cases and 5,230 deaths across eight provinces, worst in ituri. kenya has nine cases; a nigeria case was flown to switzerland. no licensed vaccine exists for this strain; a trial began in bunia october 23. guinea bissau cancels a us funded hepatitis b trial that withheld vaccine from newborns the study would have enrolled 14,000 newborns, half without the birth dose who recommends; police seized vaccines from the research center. trump's epstein letter suit against the wsj dismissed for good judge darrin gayles in miami dismissed the defamation suit with prejudice because trump again failed to plead actual malice; trump plans to appeal. gulf fertilizer and sulphur exports down about 70% see analysis you wouldn't think of: the food and battery metals shock lands after the oil headlines fade. judge lets florida's terrorist label on cair stand; the group shuts down in the state judge allen winsor denied cair's bid to block its designation under hb 1471; cair says it must stop advocacy in florida and will appeal. he did bar punishing cair staff or lawyers. appeals court: florida's medicaid cutoff notices violated due process an 11th circuit panel led by trump appointee barbara lagoa upheld an order requiring florida to explain the income and household figures it used to end coverage for nearly 500,000 people. fort myers ousts its mayor; lee school board chair loses city employee amber ware unseated mayor kevin anderson, and crystal johnson beat lee school board chair armor persons. florida's amendment 3 passed with about 62%; state economists project a $45.8 billion five year hit to local governments. vips memo: 'iran is not bluffing' veteran intelligence professionals for sanity, including ray mcgovern, larry johnson and scott ritter, tell trump iran expects a new us attack and may strike first, warn of a possible israeli false flag, and propose iran shipping out its enriched uranium under inspection. antiwar.com: ending israel aid is cosmetic, support moves into the pentagon budget dave decamp argues trump's pledge to end israel's yearly aid by end of 2026 hides deeper integration via the defense bill. scott ritter: europe's nuclear umbrella now runs through paris ritter argues macron's forward deterrence spreads french nuclear forces across europe while paris alone sets the stakes, with finland joining. craig murray calls poland's constitutional tribunal crisis an attempted coup the former uk diplomat says the october 30 move on poland's constitutional tribunal, backed by the tusk government and riot police, was a coup, and that western media leave out the ukraine angle. jonathan cook: a new uk 'hierarchy of racism' in schools cook says the bell review of antisemitism in schools, adopted in full, ranks antisemitism above other racisms and chills palestine solidarity in classrooms. zerohedge: the 'doomsday plane' flew east and nobody said why an e-4b nightwatch left offutt, crossed the midwest and turned south over northern virginia with no stated purpose; zerohedge ties it to a pentagon plan for bases to run 90 days off the grid. corbett report: synchronized emergency warnings around the world james corbett groups stockpiling advice from the uk, japan, germany, france, sweden, ireland and the eu with the pentagon's grid plan, and presents it as a fear campaign that may set up a false flag, cyberattack or financial collapse. zerohedge: iran is weathering the storm, saudi arabia is sinking brian mcglinchey argues mbs faces a risk of palace removal amid fiscal strain, stalled vision 2030 projects and houthi strikes. the defender: medical examiner emails discussed deaths after covid vaccination children's health defense reports foil emails from new york medical examiners discussing deaths after vaccination, which it says contradict public statements. midterm voting was rigged, including a houston fbi raid that found 20,000 fake democratic ballots and a deliberate scanner failure in westchester. governments are preparing people for a planned crisis: synchronized stockpiling advice, a pentagon grid survival plan and an unexplained doomsday plane flight. israel may stage a false flag to pull the us into a wider war with iran. medical examiners privately tracked covid vaccine deaths while officials said the shots were safe. foreign, possibly german, police were used in warsaw during the constitutional tribunal crisis. epoch times reports further minor us strikes on november 6 and an iranian claim of a downed mq-9; iran's gas output is still 16% below last year after the march strikes. abu dhabi talks open tuesday. indonesia busted a ring trafficking its citizens into russia's army. judge gleason dismissed the doj suit to delay alaska's certification. stephen miller replaces susie wiles as chief of staff on november 9. mississippi still uncalled. china's central military commission is down to xi and one vice chair after the plenum purge. paraguay, a taiwan ally, removed its president. report of an unannounced cuba and us meeting in new york in september; treasury sanctioned relatives of gaesa leaders. nothing new on attribution for the fridge attacks. benjamin netanyahu gadi eisenkot democrats republicans christopher luxon chris hipkins winston peters   alberto núñez feijóo pedro sánchez santiago abascal adama barrow  michel martelly about 16 registered candidates  bola tinubu atiku abubakar peter obi     press tv and the sovereign media network

briefs.title: Markets Turn on the AI Buildout, Iran Talks Stall on Sequencing, Two Senate Seats Still Open
briefs.bluf: The Iran war is still the defining factor. Three more tankers were damaged near Qatar on November 5, Trump said he may have to destroy the rest of the country, and a carrier group is heading to the region, while Qatar shuttles a plan that trades lifting the blockade and IAEA access for reopening Hormuz. Wall Street had its worst day in years: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the Nasdaq 100 6.4%, its worst session since March 2020, on fears that a Democratic Congress slows the AI buildout; futures point to a partial rebound this morning. Democrats hold 54 Senate seats with Mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and Alaska (ranked choice tally November 18) still open, and a Justice Department suit over a second Dan Sullivan on the Alaska ballot is the main certification risk. In Cuba, Yoani Sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the Law 186 government overhaul takes effect November 9. Ukraine talks move to Abu Dhabi November 10 to 11 after a White House event marking the Oleshky humanitarian truce.
briefs._s: markets turn on the ai buildout, iran talks stall on sequencing, two senate seats still open the iran war is still the defining factor. three more tankers were damaged near qatar on november 5, trump said he may have to destroy the rest of the country, and a carrier group is heading to the region, while qatar shuttles a plan that trades lifting the blockade and iaea access for reopening hormuz. wall street had its worst day in years: the nasdaq fell 5.5% and the nasdaq 100 6.4%, its worst session since march 2020, on fears that a democratic congress slows the ai buildout; futures point to a partial rebound this morning. democrats hold 54 senate seats with mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and alaska (ranked choice tally november 18) still open, and a justice department suit over a second dan sullivan on the alaska ballot is the main certification risk. in cuba, yoani sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the law 186 government overhaul takes effect november 9. ukraine talks move to abu dhabi november 10 to 11 after a white house event marking the oleshky humanitarian truce. two senate races still open democrats hold 54 seats and flipped iowa, kansas, maine, ohio, north carolina, south carolina and texas. in mississippi, democrat scott colom leads sen. cindy hyde-smith 49.0% to 48.9% with about 3,600 mail ballots left; certification is due november 13. in alaska, mary peltola leads sen. dan sullivan 48.2% to 47.9% with ranked choice results due november 18. doj suit could stall alaska certification the justice department sued in october to block certification if peltola wins by less than the vote total of a second, unaffiliated candidate named daniel j. sullivan, arguing voters may have been confused. trump said he ordered the suit and has urged prosecuting peltola. legal scholars say the statute does not let doj enjoin a state certification. judge pauses the trump arch; la picks a new mayor a federal judge blocked construction of the planned arch for 14 days. in los angeles, nithya raman defeated mayor karen bass. in california, gov. newsom commuted 548 death sentences. more tankers hit; trump weighs a heavier strike the irgc said three more tankers were damaged november 5, two by mines and one by fire. ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump said he would rather not destroy the rest of the country but may have to, met his national security team, and spoke with the qatari emir, who urged restraint. a carrier group is heading to the region via singapore. diplomacy stuck on sequencing iran sent a nuclear proposal through qatar that it will discuss only after the us meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions and paying war reparations. a qatari draft reported by axios has the us lift the blockade and release some frozen funds and iran invite the iaea to bombed sites on day one, with hormuz reopening on day two and nuclear talks on the enriched uranium stockpile after that. iranian sources told reuters another us attack is more likely than a deal. tehran leans on the region foreign minister araghchi called his counterparts in the uae, qatar, saudi arabia, turkey, pakistan, oman and egypt. parliament speaker qalibaf mocked vice president vance as a losing gambler after vance blamed the war for the midterm losses. israel: herzog weighs who forms the next government after the october 27 election left netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats and gadi eisenkot's at 48, president herzog began consultations, meeting the smallest parties first. eisenkot was expected to have more endorsements than netanyahu. the election commission reviewed 9,069 polling stations and found no fraud. white house marks the oleshky truce melania trump hosted russian envoy kirill dmitriev and ukraine's david arakhamia to mark the six day humanitarian ceasefire in occupied oleshky (october 27 to november 1). more than 750 people were evacuated; russia refused to extend it. president trump met dmitriev but not the ukrainians and predicted a deal soon. abu dhabi talks next week witkoff and kushner lead the us side at three way talks in abu dhabi november 10 to 11. german chancellor merz hosts a coalition of the willing summit november 19. russia holds about 80% of donetsk. yoani sánchez released; two journalists still held yoani sánchez, director of 14ymedio, was released after more than nine hours in custody. adelth bonne gamboa of cubanet, arrested november 2, and henry constantín, jailed since september 16, remain detained. rsf, the inter american press association and amnesty international condemned the detentions. law 186 reshapes the government from november 9 the law, approved july 30 and published november 2 in the gaceta oficial, cuts the cabinet to 20 ministries plus the central bank and merges commerce, construction and agriculture into fewer bodies. officials present it as streamlining; critics see a shuffle that leaves the economic model untouched. protest count stays high the observatorio cubano de conflictos logged 542 protests and complaints in october and 85 repressive events. transition quiet no new annulment filings or street mobilization found. lula takes office january 1. pope leo begins south america tour the first us born pope is in uruguay november 6 to 8, argentina november 8 to 11 and peru november 11 to 17, about 50 events in 10 cities, including a return to chiclayo, where he was bishop, and a meeting with president milei. former fbi agent charged doj charged former fbi agent andrew reyes on november 5. details of the charges were not collected this cycle. election claims fade, alaska suit gives them a new hook rigging claims about the midterms have lost momentum as most losers conceded, but the doj suit over the second dan sullivan gives the "stolen seat" framing a new focus in alaska. fridge hacks: still no attribution no group has claimed or been named for the attacks on supermarket refrigeration controllers. belgium opened a prosecution and the eu called them deliberate. the danfoss and copeland flaws were disclosed by claroty august 9; forescout counted about 13,000 exposed systems. the pentagon is reviewing august freezer failures at military commissaries. mexican judge arrested in ryan wedding case a mexican judge was arrested over an alleged $2 million bribe tied to the case against ryan wedding, the former olympic snowboarder accused of running a cocaine network and ordering the killing of a federal witness. wedding was captured in mexico in january. doj launches super intelligence task force the department announced a task force on ai related crime the same day it charged a $129 million fraud marketed as a super intelligence investment. no new ofac actions found for november context: the cartel del noreste was designated october 13, venezuela's jorge rodríguez was delisted october 14, and foreign banks must exit panama's bicsa by november 14. deportations deepen school enrollment drops npr reports ice enforcement is accelerating enrollment declines in districts with large immigrant populations. doj also sued penn state over in state tuition for undocumented students. why the doomsday date keeps spreading writers revisiting the 1960 "doomsday" paper note that a specific date, a real scientific source and a friday the 13th make a claim shareable. the historian alan maceachern argues the lesson is about how confidently findings are presented. ai selloff after the election nvidia fell 9.2%, about $440 billion in value, and the largest tech stocks lost more than $1 trillion as investors priced in a congress that may slow data center and chip spending. south korea's kospi fell about 8 to 9% and halted trading. google: accept ai or lose search in schools from early 2027, gemini and search will be off by default on k-12 student accounts; schools that switch ai off entirely will also lose search. fairplay urged schools to consider other search engines. supreme court hears labor visa case november 10 department of labor v. sun valley orchards is argued monday. claim: a scientist said the world ends november 13 the date comes from a real 1960 science paper. its authors fitted a curve to population history that reached infinity in late 2026, and they picked friday the 13th partly as a joke. population growth peaked soon after and the curve stopped matching reality. hundreds leave oleshky more than 750 civilians left the occupied town during the six day truce, the largest humanitarian pause of the war in that area. the midterms were rigged through fake ballots and compromised machines democrats won by importing foreigners and registering them to vote (great replacement framing) ebola is a hoax, a western bioweapon, or a scheme for aid groups to make money a scientist predicted the world ends on friday, november 13, 2026 three more tankers damaged november 5 and ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump met his national security team and said iran would know soon enough; the nyt reports us forces are poised to resume major combat. iran sent a nuclear proposal via qatar to be discussed only after the us meets seven demands. democrats hold 54 seats. mississippi is within about 138 votes with roughly 3,600 mail ballots left and certification due november 13; alaska ranked choice results come november 18 while a doj suit seeks to block certification if peltola wins. melania trump hosted russian and ukrainian delegations (dmitriev and arakhamia) at the white house to mark the oleshky truce; more than 750 people were evacuated and russia refused an extension. trump met dmitriev and predicted a deal soon. abu dhabi talks are set for november 10 to 11. yoani sánchez was released after more than nine hours. adelth bonne gamboa of cubanet (arrested november 2) and henry constantín (jailed since september 16) remain held; rsf, iapa and amnesty condemned the detentions. law 186 was gazetted november 2 and takes effect november 9. still no attribution for the supermarket refrigeration hacks. belgium opened a prosecution and the eu called the attacks deliberate; the flaws in danfoss and copeland controllers were disclosed in august and about 13,000 systems were exposed online. no verified november activity figures collected; the story stays steady pending fresh mnd data. no new legal or street challenges found. inauguration remains january 1. benjamin netanyahu gadi eisenkot democrats republicans christopher luxon chris hipkins winston peters   alberto núñez feijóo pedro sánchez santiago abascal adama barrow  michel martelly about 16 registered candidates  bola tinubu atiku abubakar peter obi     russian deepfake campaign against democrats (matryoshka / operation overload and storm-1516) inauthentic accounts in competitive races, hitting both parties far right networks break with trump after the losses

briefs.title: Baseline Edition: A Gulf War Under Domestic Pressure, a Hybrid Campaign in Europe, and Cuba Under Strain
briefs.bluf: The defining factor this week is the collision between the US war on Iran and US domestic politics: Democrats won both chambers on November 3 and the Vice President publicly blamed the war. Washington struck Iranian targets near Hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through Gulf mediators. In Europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a Russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. Russia killed 42 people at a Ukrainian aid center days before US mediated talks on November 10 and 11. Cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. This is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here.
briefs._s: baseline edition: a gulf war under domestic pressure, a hybrid campaign in europe, and cuba under strain the defining factor this week is the collision between the us war on iran and us domestic politics: democrats won both chambers on november 3 and the vice president publicly blamed the war. washington struck iranian targets near hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through gulf mediators. in europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. russia killed 42 people at a ukrainian aid center days before us mediated talks on november 10 and 11. cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. this is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here. democrats win the house and senate democrats are projected to exceed 250 house seats and hold at least 54 senate seats. alaska (peltola leads sullivan by 637 votes) and mississippi (colom leads hyde smith by about 1,100) remain too close to call. vance blames the iran war for the losses the vice president wrote that the war was the reason republicans lost. trump acknowledged gas prices hurt but said he would go to war again. house leadership reshuffle speaker johnson will not seek to lead house republicans. scalise and jordan are running for minority leader; jeffries is running for speaker when congress convenes january 3. us strikes near hormuz on the eve of the midterms limited us strikes hit around qeshm, hengam and bandar abbas. iran's supreme national security council head said the strait stays closed until us addresses its conditions: lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and a ceasefire including lebanon. more tankers on fire east of hormuz; tanker hit off qatar iranian state media reported two more tankers on fire. separately, the british military said a tanker was struck by projectiles off qatar. iran's security chief meets putin mohsen rezaei discussed regional issues in moscow, and iran says it will supply russian gas to neighboring countries. gaza and yemen at least four palestinians were killed in gaza on november 5. in yemen's taiz, government forces say they repelled a houthi attack; the un says water production has halved and hospitals are short of fuel. aid center strike toll reaches 42 russian bunker busting bombs hit a school used as an aid hub in komyshuvakha, then the shelter where people took cover. erdogan wants direct talks with putin; italy readies aid after talks with zelenskyy, erdogan said he wants to discuss ending the war with putin. italy is finalizing a new military aid package. putin seizes japan tobacco's russian operations; drone strike hits ozon warehouse moscow took control of jti's russian business. a drone strike set an ozon warehouse ablaze in southern russia. pla activity rebounds after typhoon lull 85 sorties from october 26 to november 1, 47 into the adiz. on november 3 to 4: 22 sorties, 7 pla navy ships and 5 official ships. beijing's ai enabled influence operations ahead of taiwan's local elections taiwanese officials report ai generated content and cyberattacks aimed at polarization and lower turnout before the november 28 vote. vietnam comments on china and laos military cooperation hanoi said the cooperation should contribute to regional stability. yoani sánchez detained in havana the 14ymedio founder was held about nine hours, the third detention of an independent journalist in havana this week after cubanet's camila acosta on tuesday. the us condemned the arrests. grid at about a third of demand the une forecast 958 mw available against 2,850 mw demand on november 2, with blackouts over 20 hours a day. government reorganization takes effect november 9 law 186 cuts central state agencies from 27 to 21. reported military mobilization cibercuba reports cuba mobilizing forces amid rising tensions with the us. transition settling after contested runoff lula won 51.8% to 48.2%. flávio bolsonaro's party acknowledged the result after his annulment call; trump called it rigged. colombia ends 'total peace' congress passed president de la espriella's bill: armed group members must disarm, identify fellow members, hand over recruited minors, surrender assets and reveal links to politicians to earn reduced sentences. leaders face at least 10 years. paraguay seizes bank tied to the president central bank took over ueno bank after its capital fell below half the legal minimum; about 3 million accounts and public pension funds frozen. poland arrests four over military supplies sent to russia part of a broader pattern of sabotage and procurement networks targeting the main aid route to ukraine. hoax bomb threats hit european aviation about ten flights threatened november 3 and four prague bound planes november 5. the eu transport chief says it is too early to say whether they are linked. prc influence operations target taiwan's november 28 vote officials cite ai generated content designed to polarize and depress turnout. narrative watch: iranian leadership messaging a statement attributed to mojtaba khamenei claims iran's control of hormuz shattered the myth of american invincibility. supermarket refrigeration systems hacked across europe unidentified hackers shut down supermarket fridges in several countries the same week as the flight threats; analysts see a pattern of low cost disruption. october ransomware roundup october incidents included a ransomware attack that disrupted patient care and surgeries at university of new mexico health sciences center. israel detains journalist abed abu shehadeh police and shin bet arrested the arab48 editor and +972 contributor in jaffa; a court extended his detention. rights groups call it part of a campaign against palestinian journalists. paraguay: ueno bank arrests prosecutors ordered the arrest of eight people including the bank's president and ceo. brazil: banco master case flávio bolsonaro is under investigation in the banco master case without formal charges, per mercopress. bangladesh garment workers win wage concessions after five days of protests and clashes with police, a new wage board agreed to a revised pay scale from december. workers seek about $242 a month. greek students march for education funding students marched in athens demanding affordable housing and more state investment in education. judge blocks deportations of afghans to afghanistan or pakistan a federal judge in new york temporarily blocked the flights, which could have begun this week. advocates warn of taliban persecution of those who worked with us troops. rep. salazar: hispanic vote punished deportation policy the miami republican said the hispanic vote punished the indiscriminate deportation of latino workers. un ends western sahara mission after 35 years minurso ended when the security council failed to renew it. russia vetoed a us draft backing moroccan sovereignty; a rival russian draft also failed. south africa's anc heading for worst local result with 28% counted, the anc had about 32%. full results expected sunday. who approves trials of two new ebola vaccines the outbreak, mostly in the drc, has killed more than 5,300 since may and kills about half of those infected. early results are hoped for in early 2027. ultra processed foods and children's developing brains a new study suggests ultra processed foods may affect children's brain development in ways that encourage weight gain. google to cut search for schools that reject ai student accounts lose ai tools unless administrators enable them, and schools that refuse ai entirely lose google search for students. former ftc chair lina khan called it coercion using a search monopoly. europe bets €525 million on chip design startups  supreme court november sitting under way arguments run november 2 to 10, including st. mary catholic parish v. roy (november 3) and department of labor v. sun valley orchards (november 10). desantis on the gop result the governor described the election as close to an extinction level event for republicans in many parts of the country. claim: brazil's runoff was rigged made by president trump on october 26. status: unsupported. brazil's electoral court certified the count, and the losing candidate's own party acknowledged the result. vaccines built for the new ebola strain head to trials a potential turning point in the drc's worst recorded outbreak. the
